screening_decisions.reason: Double-blind randomized trial of theophylline (as aminophylline) vs placebo in 46 patients with acute ischemic stroke. Treatment was administered during 3 days starting at admission. Meets all selection criteria: randomized design, theophylline/analogue intervention, placebo control, acute stroke population, and treatment within one week of onset.

Double-blind randomized trial of intravenous aminophylline vs placebo in 79 patients with acute cerebral infarction. Meets all selection criteria: randomized design, aminophylline intervention (theophylline analogue), placebo control, acute stroke population. Treatment timing consistent with acute phase.

This is an open-label, single-arm, dose-escalation study, NOT a randomized controlled trial. No placebo or control group. While it involves caffeine (an analogue) in acute stroke patients with treatment within 6 hours, it fails the fundamental requirement of being a randomized trial with control comparison.

Not a randomized trial of theophylline/analogue as primary intervention. Study focuses on vincamin (Pervincamine) with only 12 of 60 subjects receiving aminophyllin as a secondary arm. Population not clearly defined as acute stroke patients. Does not meet selection criteria.

Randomized crossover trial of caffeine vs placebo, but patients are described as 'recovering from' acute ischaemic stroke rather than in the acute phase. The selection criteria require treatment started within one week of stroke onset. This study appears to be conducted in the recovery phase, not the acute phase within one week of onset.

Randomized crossover trial of caffeine vs placebo, but patients are described as 'recovering from' acute ischaemic stroke. Similar to Study 5, this does not meet the timing criterion of treatment started within one week of stroke onset. The study focuses on cerebral blood flow changes rather than clinical outcomes in the acute phase.

Not a randomized controlled trial. This is a physiological study examining cerebral blood flow changes with aminophylline infusion. No control/placebo group comparison, and population not clearly defined as acute stroke patients. Does not meet selection criteria.

Animal study conducted in cats with experimentally induced middle cerebral artery occlusion. Selection criteria require human trials in people with acute ischaemic stroke. Does not meet population criterion.
Animal study conducted in anesthetized dogs. Selection criteria require human trials in people with acute ischaemic stroke. Does not meet population criterion.

This appears to be a review or commentary article, not a randomized controlled trial. The abstract references historical reports and notes that 'convincing controlled series are still lacking.' Does not meet the study design criterion of being a randomized trial.
